clue.text: Match pipe that's used in experiment supervised by 14 across, perhaps

definitions.text: used in experiment supervised by 14 across, perhaps
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the glass vessel

blocks.note: a test match is an international cricket fixture, so Test can stand for a match

explanation.surface: A pipe used in a lab demonstration run by a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 14 across, the science master, who supervises school experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow glass vessel is the standard piece of laboratory glassware for holding chemicals in a school experiment.

clue.text: Strike the short Scouser's mate

blocks.note: wack is Liverpool slang for a friend; a Scouser is a Liverpudlian

explanation.surface: Hitting the Liverpudlian's pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard smacking blow, a synonym of strike as a verb or noun.

clue.text: Unfortunately tripping up tackling square dance

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
a tackler grabs hold of something, so this word wraps around the next

blocks.note: alas expresses that something is unfortunate
S is an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Sadly someone stumbles while doing a square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square dance' looks like one thing, but square is the inserted letter and dance the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Latin American partner dance named after the music it is danced to.

clue.text: Study inside heart of match factory reveals a wearisome routine

indicators.note: inside means the study goes within what follows
the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
the centre letter of the five

explanation.surface: Revision done in the middle of a match factory proves dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match factory' looks like one place; match gives a letter and factory a word, and the study sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine walked on without getting anywhere, figuratively any monotonous grind.

clue.text: A means of leverage to disqualify 'winning' golf shot

blocks.note: to bar someone is to disqualify them
a chip is a short lofted golf shot

explanation.surface: A golfer's winning stroke ruled out as a lever in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offered or held back in negotiation to gain an advantage over the other side.

clue.text: Person, for example, associated with a wine shop

blocks.note: bod is informal British for a person
the usual abbreviation, from Latin exempli gratia

explanation.surface: Someone who has some link with a wine merchant's.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish word adopted into English for a small shop or cellar selling wine.

clue.text: Shell female got rid of in past

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: former means earlier, of the past
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman discarded a seashell long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: An ormer is an edible shellfish, the abalone, found around the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is a sea snail valued for its ear-shaped shell, so a shell stands for it.

clue.text: Bass guitarist released new titles

indicators.note: something released is set loose, so the letters break free into a new order

explanation.surface: A bass player put out fresh tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: John Entwistle was the bass guitarist of The Who.
explanation.definitionFit: John Entwistle played bass guitar in the British rock band The Who.

clue.text: Fitzgerald returned with grisly tale

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the name is read from the end

explanation.surface: A singer came back with a gruesome story.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitzgerald could be the novelist F Scott; the reversal needs the jazz singer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A story whose characters and events stand for a hidden moral meaning, a kind of tale.

clue.text: A part of geese I'd prepared?

definitions.text: A part of geese I'd prepared?

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made up from raw ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether a portion of goose is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: the dish is made from part of a goose, its liver.
explanation.definitionFit: This delicacy is a paste made from the fattened liver of a goose, a part of the bird prepared for eating.

clue.text: Reportedly undisciplined playwright

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by the sound of the word

explanation.surface: A dramatist said to be unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright of The Importance of Being Earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde is a famous example of an Irish dramatist.

clue.text: Stones in the way derailed lead tram - none on board

indicators.note: a passenger on board is carried inside the vehicle, so this letter goes within the others
a derailed vehicle is thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Obstruction on the track: a tram with nobody aboard has come off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: Road metal is British for broken stone used to surface roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushed rock laid as the base of a road is literally stone in the roadway.

clue.text: Female spies receiving praise

indicators.note: the spies take in the next word, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A woman agent being commended by the secret service.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so it can be clued by a word for a woman.

clue.text: Making a mistake about a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: about means around, so the phrase wraps the small word

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Getting something wrong regarding a bit of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament worn on the lobe of the ear is a common item of jewellery.

clue.text: Dispose of a semi - crescent stinks!

indicators.note: to dispose things is to arrange them, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: An order to get rid of a semicircular thing that smells foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinks' looks like a verb; it is old British public-school slang for chemistry, and so for the teacher of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils nicknamed the chemistry teacher Stinks after the smells of the lab.

clue.text: Injured tiger seen in national park

indicators.note: an injured thing is damaged and twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wounded big cat spotted on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: Tigers are Asian, so the injured one would be lost in this African reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Serengeti is a famous wildlife reserve in Tanzania, an example of a national park.

clue.text: Union soldiers during a salute

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the soldiers sit within the salute

blocks.note: soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: Federal troops on parade during a salute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union soldiers' suggests the American Civil War, but Union is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Accord between parties, a coming together of minds, is a union in the sense of concord.

clue.text: One member legally acceptable, it's understood

explanation.surface: A single MP's conduct is lawful, it seems agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Implied without being stated outright, which is what tacitly understood means.

clue.text: On my arm in role, dizzy actress

indicators.note: dizzy means whirling and confused, so the letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained starlet clinging to someone's arm in a part.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hollywood star was famous for playing dizzy blondes, so the indicator fits her image.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was a celebrated American film star of the 1950s.

clue.text: Constant interference

blocks.note: second meaning: crackle on a radio signal

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like nonstop meddling; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means fixed or unchanging; as a noun it is the crackling noise that disturbs radio reception.

clue.text: Eccentric in a cult, bonkers

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and out of the normal pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crank in a sect who has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like the definition, but it is the anagram signal; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone behaving in a wildly crazy way; the answer works as an adjective here.

clue.text: Dog food about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the food wraps the letter

blocks.note: tack is slang for food, as in hard tack
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Pet food that is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog food' looks like one noun phrase, but dog is a verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, and to track is to trail or pursue.

clue.text: Stylish English stage worker

blocks.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A smart English stagehand in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage worker' looks like one theatre job; it splits into a leg of a journey and an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and refined in appearance, which is what being stylish means.

clue.text: Fury shown as lid comes off crate

indicators.note: removing a lid takes away the top, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a crate and a banger are both British slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: Rage displayed when the top is prised off a packing case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crate' suggests a box, but here it is an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is extreme rage, and the answer is the general word for that strong feeling.

clue.text: A gallant French actor and singer

blocks.note: first meaning: a knight or chivalrous man
second meaning: Maurice, star of Gigi

explanation.surface: A chivalrous French entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for knight, a gallant cavalier; it is also the surname of the Parisian performer Maurice.

clue.text: Set of rowers showing power, though not having won

indicators.note: not having something means it is missing, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for won in sports results

explanation.surface: A rowing crew pulling strongly but failing to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat crewed by eight oarsmen is itself called an eight.

clue.text: Little boy, after short time, becomes difficult

indicators.note: after places the boy second, following the other piece

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Ricky is a pet form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: A small child turning awkward after a brief spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard to deal with or awkward, a synonym of difficult.

clue.text: Mysterious coteries formed

indicators.note: formed means shaped into something new, so the letters are made into another word

explanation.surface: Secretive cliques have been set up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits: coteries are exclusive groups, often with esoteric interests.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood only by a small initiated circle, hence obscure or mysterious.
